pageCache.text:
Our vision is to achieve excellence in all that we do. In doing so, we aim to prepare our pupils for the rapidly growing world in the 21st century.
Hello There!
Welcome to Darul Hadis Latifiah, Secondary School, College & Title Madrasah
Contact US
0208 980 2673
Follow Us
Pupils truly value their education and want to succeed.
They are motivated and have ambitious goals for their futures.
They work with diligence in class and try their best.
WHY STUDY WITH US?
Find out why Darul Hadis Latifiah is the ideal school to produce the next generation of Muslim leaders.
ACHIEVEMENTS AND DESTINATIONS
Discover how our school provides a platform for our students to achieve success in every field.
SCHOOL ADMISSIONS
Our admissions process is very simple. Apply today to secure a place for your child.
SCHOOL PROSPECTUS
Our prospectus provides comprehensive information about key aspects of our school.
A few words about the School
Darul Hadis Latifiah is one of the oldest Islamic secondary schools in the UK, founded in 1978. We offer a comprehensive educational experience that integrates the National Curriculum with Islamic studies, fostering both academic excellence and spiritual growth.
We are committed to delivering excellence.
Our school is dedicated to serving the community, both locally and nationally.
We motivate our students to ASPIRE high and reach their full potential, both academically and personally.
We expect our students to become sources of INSPIRATION and make a difference in the world around them.
We emphasise the importance of students RESPECT themselves, their peers, teachers, and the broader community.
Academic Programs
The Islamic Higher Education (IHE) curriculum at Darul Hadis Latifiah spans four years, with each year building upon the last to deepen the students' understanding of the Islamic sciences. Below is a brief description of the subjects taught across the programme, structured year by year:
KS3 & GCSE
At Darul Hadis Latifiah, we offer a well-rounded curriculum that blends both the UK National Curriculum and a comprehensive Islamic education, to ensure that our students receive the best of both worlds.
ALIM COURSE
Our Islamic Higher Education (IHE) curriculum is an immersive programme designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of the classical Islamic sciences.
HIFZ COURSE
Our structured Hifz programme is thoughtfully designed to guide committed students through the process of memorising the Noble Qur'an in its entirety over a period of four years.
Recent & Upcoming Events
26
Football Tournament
What Students Says
“My time at Darul Hadis Latifiah was very successful, both during my secondary studies as well as further studies. My success was primarily down to dedicated teachers who were committed in bringing the best out of me. Subsequently, I enrolled at Kingston College where I graduated with a degree in pharmacy. Following my graduation, I was fortunate to be employed as a pharmacist for the NHS. I still consider Darul Hadis Latifiah to be the foundation my success.”
Saied Ahmed
“I thoroughly enjoyed my time studying in Darul Hadis Latifiah. The atmosphere created by both the teachers and the students enabled me to benefit not only academically but also shaped me as a person. The teachers helped me to achieve the best grades and equipped me with the right skills in order to further my education in university. I will always be in debt to the teachers and staff members in this school.”
Asaduzzaman Repon

Admission Procedure
Admission Procedure
If you are interested in enrolling your child at Darul Hadis Latifiah, our admissions process is very simple:
1.Complete the Application Form
Complete and submit the application form online. Please ensure you fill in all the details correctly.
After receiving your application, we will contact you to schedule an admissions test for your child in Maths and English. This test helps us assess your child’s academic readiness. We will also require a copy of a recent school report from your child’s current school.
3.Notification of Results
Within a week of the test, we will notify you of the outcome. If a place is available, we will offer it to your child straight away. If not, they may be placed on a waiting list.
If you have any questions or need further assistance, feel free to contact us. We look forward to welcoming your child to Darul Hadis Latifiah!

Alim Course Admissions
If you are interested in joining our Alim course at Darul Hadis Latifiah, please ensure that you meet the following criteria:
1. Eligibility
Prospective students must have completed their GCSEs with at least a pass in both Maths and English.
2. Fluency in English
It is essential for students to demonstrate a sufficient level of fluency in English to participate fully in our programs. Regrettably, we are unable to accept students who do not meet this criterion.
3. UK Nationality
Students must be UK nationals, as we are unable to accept international students at this time.

Careers Education
Careers Education
At Darul Hadis Latifiah, we are committed to providing our students with comprehensive careers education and guidance, starting from Year 7 and continuing through to their final year. We believe in equipping our students with the knowledge, skills, and opportunities needed to make informed decisions about their future, whether they choose to pursue higher education or enter the workforce.
Individual Tailored Guidance
From the moment students begin their journey at Darul Hadis Latifiah, they receive one-to-one career guidance that is tailored to their individual aspirations, strengths, and interests. This personalised approach ensures that each student is supported in identifying potential career paths and setting achievable goals. Regular career interviews with dedicated staff help students stay on track and explore their options throughout their school life.
Workshops and External Support
We regularly organise a variety of career-focused workshops to help students develop the skills they need for the modern workplace. These workshops cover essential topics such as writing CVs, filling out job applications, and preparing for interviews. External agencies are also invited to assist our students in building strong CVs and taking part in mock interviews to prepare them for real-world scenarios.
Work Experience in Year 10
As part of their career development, all Year 10 students are offered work experience placements. This practical exposure gives students a taste of the professional environment and helps them develop key employability skills such as teamwork, communication, and problem-solving. Our partnerships with local businesses and organisations ensure students gain valuable experience in sectors that align with their career interests.
University Visits and Career Fairs
To inspire and broaden students’ horizons, we arrange visits to prestigious universities across London and beyond. These trips allow students to explore different higher education options and hear from admissions staff about what it takes to succeed at university level. In addition to this, we organise attendance at career fairs, where students have the opportunity to meet representatives from various industries, gaining insight into different career paths and emerging opportunities.
Guest Speakers and Assemblies
Throughout the academic year, we invite professionals from diverse industries to speak during assemblies and special events. These guest speakers provide invaluable insights into their respective fields, share their career journeys, and offer advice on the skills and qualifications needed to succeed. This direct interaction with industry professionals helps students better understand the world of work and the range of careers available to them.
One of the highlights of our careers programme is our dedicated Enterprise Week, where students engage in activities that explore various aspects of the working world, including entrepreneurship, finance, and project management. This hands-on experience encourages students to think creatively and develop their problem-solving skills while learning about business and enterprise.
At Darul Hadis Latifiah, we strive to ensure that each student leaves us with the confidence and skills necessary to thrive in their chosen career path. By offering a wide range of careers education opportunities, we support our students in becoming successful, well-rounded individuals who are ready to make meaningful contributions to society.

pageCache.text:
Reading and Literacy
Reading and Literacy
At Darul Hadis Latifiah, we place a strong emphasis on reading and literacy, understanding the vital role they play in shaping our students' academic success, personal growth, and future opportunities. We believe that fostering a love for reading from an early age not only enhances language skills but also opens doors to critical thinking, creativity, and self-expression.
Promoting a Reading Culture
One of the ways we encourage this at our school is by making it mandatory for all students to carry a reading book with them throughout the school day. This policy ensures that students always have access to reading material, and they are given time to read daily, particularly in the morning before tutorial sessions when they gather in the hall for a quiet reading period. This regular practice cultivates both a habit of reading and an appreciation for literature in students’ everyday routines.
Dedicated Reading and Literacy Lessons
In Years 7 and 8, we provide dedicated reading and literacy lessons, where students engage in guided reading, vocabulary-building exercises, and comprehension activities. These lessons aim to enhance students' reading fluency, understanding, and critical thinking, while exposing them to a variety of genres and writing styles. Through these sessions, students explore both fiction and non-fiction texts, allowing them to develop skills necessary for success in subjects across the curriculum.
Visits to Local Libraries
To further nurture students' interest in reading, we organise regular visits to local libraries, where they can explore a wide range of books and other resources. These trips not only support students in finding reading material that matches their interests, but also teach them essential research and library skills. We encourage students to take advantage of these library visits by borrowing books, which helps foster independence and responsibility for their own learning.
World Book Day Celebrations
At Darul Hadis Latifiah, we celebrate World Book Day annually, a highlight of our literacy programme. Students and staff are encouraged to immerse themselves in literature through a variety of activities. This celebration of books and reading is a wonderful opportunity for students to see reading as fun and engaging, while also broadening their exposure to different kinds of literature.
Competitions and Prizes
We believe that recognising students’ efforts in reading and writing helps to motivate and inspire them. Therefore, we hold half-termly writing and speaking competitions, where students are encouraged to showcase their creativity and writing abilities. These competitions cover a wide range of themes and allow students to develop their communication skills, both in writing and public speaking. Prizes are awarded to the best readers and writers, providing an additional incentive for students to push themselves and aim for excellence.
Fostering Literacy Beyond Reading
Our literacy programme extends beyond reading and into the realms of writing and speaking, recognising the importance of well-rounded communication skills. Students are taught to articulate their thoughts clearly and confidently, both in writing and verbally. The half-termly competitions also include public speaking events, where students can practice presenting their ideas to an audience, an essential skill for future academic and professional success.
Inspiring Lifelong Learners
Ultimately, our goal is to instil a love for reading and a strong foundation in literacy that stays with our students for life. We believe that students who develop these skills early on are better equipped to succeed academically, think critically, and engage meaningfully with the world around them. By integrating reading into the daily lives of our students and offering varied literacy-focused activities, we are committed to developing confident, articulate learners who are prepared to excel both in school and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values and The Equality Act 2010 – Darul Hadis Latifiah
pageCache.text:
British Values and The Equality Act 2010
At Darul Hadis, we actively promote the four fundamental British Values, namely:
– individual liberty
– mutual respect for and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs and for those without faith.
At Darul Hadis, we believe that all people living in England are subject to the law of the land.

Islamic Curriculum
Islamic Studies Curriculum
At Darul Hadis Latifiah, the Islamic studies curriculum is designed to provide a deep, systematic understanding of essential Islamic sciences from Year 7 to Year 11. Each subject is carefully structured to develop students’ knowledge of their faith and spiritual practice, equipping them with a strong foundation for both their religious and personal lives. Below is a brief summary of the key subjects covered:
Qirat & Tajweed
Qirat and Tajweed teach students the proper rules and techniques for reciting the Qur’an. Tajweed focuses on pronunciation, rhythm, and phonetics, ensuring that students recite the Qur’an in accordance with classical standards. Through Qirat, students develop fluency and mastery in reciting the Qur’an with clarity and beauty, enhancing both their understanding and connection with the holy text.
Qur’an Shareef
In this subject, students learn the meanings and lessons from key surahs (chapters) of the Qur’an that are essential for everyday life. The emphasis is placed on understanding the meaning, context and significance of the verses, as well as their practical applications. Students develop a deep connection with the Qur’an, learning how its guidance can be applied to improve their lives and strengthen their faith.
Hadith Shareef
This subject focuses on the teachings of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his guidance on how to live as a better Muslim. Through the study of selected hadiths, students learn about key aspects of moral character, ethics, and the principles of good behaviour in daily life. The curriculum encourages students to embody the noble qualities that define a true Muslim, such as honesty, kindness, and humility.
Each of these subjects is taught systematically over the course of five years, from Year 7 to Year 11, providing students with a comprehensive and in-depth Islamic education that complements their academic studies.
Fiqh
This subject focuses on the essentials of worship and Islamic jurisprudence according to the Hanafi school of thought. Students learn about the proper methods of prayer (Salah), purification (Tahara), fasting (Sawm), charity (Zakat), and other important aspects of day-to-day worship. The curriculum equips students with the knowledge needed to practice their religion with accuracy and devotion.
Aqeedah
Aqeedah covers the core beliefs of a Muslim, such as belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Day of Judgment, and divine predestination. Students systematically learn about the pillars of Islamic faith, ensuring they have a strong theological foundation. This subject strengthens students’ understanding of their beliefs and helps them develop a sound Islamic worldview.
Islamic History
This subject covers the Seerah, or biography of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, as well as the lives of previous prophets and the Companions (Sahaba). Students explore key events in Islamic history, including the revelations, battles, and the establishment of the early Muslim community. By studying the lives of these exemplary figures, students gain inspiration and learn valuable lessons for their own personal development.

Alim Course Details
The Islamic Higher Education (IHE) curriculum at Darul Hadis Latifiah spans four years, with each year building upon the last to deepen the students' understanding of the Islamic sciences. Below is a brief description of the subjects taught across the programme, structured year by year:
Alim (1st Year)
A foundational study of the sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Students engage with selected Hadith from Mishkat, learning to understand the methodology behind their collection as well the chapters pertaining to Iman (Faith).
This subject introduces students to the science of Hadith classification, covering the principles behind evaluating the authenticity of narrations and understanding their chain of transmission.
Focuses on the essentials of worship according to the Hanafi school of thought, covering subjects like purification, prayer, fasting, and Zakat based on the well-acclaimed Mukhtasar al-Quduri.
In this subject, students focus on the translation of the final 10 surahs and Surah al-Baqarah, learning the linguistic and interpretative nuances.
A comprehensive study of the rules of Arabic grammar to enhance students' ability to understand classical Islamic texts in their original language.
Students are introduced to key works in Arabic literature, developing their ability to comprehend and analyse classical Arabic prose and poetry.
This course covers the early history of Islam, with particular focus on the life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
A study of Islamic laws related to inheritance, focusing on the division of estates according to Islamic guidelines.
Alim (2nd Year)
Continuing from the first year, students delve deeper into the Hadith of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, focusing on the chapters of Adab (Etiquette).
A more advanced study of Hadith sciences, exploring the grading of narrations and the various types of chains of transmission (Isnad).
In this year, students study more complex aspects of Islamic jurisprudence, particularly in areas such as Hajj, marriage, and divorce.
Introduces students to the fundamental principles of deriving Islamic law (Shariah) from the Qur’an and Sunnah, using Usul al-Shashi, a well-known primer.
A continuation of Arabic grammar studies, focusing on more complex linguistic structures and their application in Islamic texts.
Further exploration of classical Arabic literature, with an emphasis on understanding complex linguistic and literary devices used in classical texts.
A more detailed study of early Islamic history, with a focus on the caliphates and the major events that shaped the Islamic world.
A foundational study of Islamic theology (Aqeedah), using the famous text by Imam Tahawi to explore the core beliefs of a Muslim.
Fadil (3rd Year)
Students continue to deepen their knowledge of the Hadith, with an emphasis on understanding their legal and spiritual implications.
Advanced study of Hadith sciences, exploring more intricate methodologies of Hadith verification and classification.
Students engage with more advanced areas of Hanafi Fiqh, delving into the rules of financial transactions, and other complex legal matters.
In this year, students study Nur al-Anwar, an advanced text on the principles of Islamic jurisprudence, providing deeper insight into the reasoning behind legal rulings, covering the chapters of Sunnah, Ijma’ and Qiyas.
Advanced grammar studies, focusing on mastering the language to read and interpret complex legal and theological texts.
Students explore classical Arabic literature in greater depth, enhancing their ability to critically engage with Islamic scholarly works.
An introduction to the interpretation of the Qur’an using the renowned commentary Tafsir al-Jalalain, which explains the meanings of the verses in a concise and clear manner, covering surahs Yasin, Saffat and Saad.
A foundational study of Islamic theology (Aqeedah), using the famous text by Imam Tahawi to explore the core beliefs of a Muslim.
This subject teaches the methodologies of interpreting the Qur’an, using classical texts such as al-Fawz al-Kabir.
A more advanced study of Islamic theology, focusing on the beliefs of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah, using Nasafiyyah.
An introduction to Islamic spirituality, focusing on personal development and purification of the soul in line with the teachings of classical scholars.
Kamil (4th Year)
In the final year, students study selections from the six major books of Hadith—Bukhari, Muslim, Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah—developing a deep understanding of the sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
An advanced study of the principles of Hadith sciences using the renowned text Nukhbah al-Fikar and its commentary Nuzhah al-Nazar, which explores the most intricate details of Hadith methodology.
Students study Tafsir al-Baidawi, one of the most respected and scholarly works on Qur’anic commentary, delving deep into the meanings and linguistic intricacies of the Qur’an.
Using al-Itqan, students study the principles and methods used by classical scholars to interpret the Qur’an and derive rulings from its verses.
The final year covers the major events and developments in Islamic history, focusing on their impact on contemporary Islamic thought.

Alim Course Introduction
Introduction
At Darul Hadis Latifiah, our Islamic Higher Education (IHE) curriculum is an advanced, immersive programme designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of the classical Islamic sciences. Rooted in the internationally renowned Dars-e-Nizami framework, this curriculum offers a structured and comprehensive education aimed at nurturing Islamic scholars who possess not only a deep mastery of traditional Islamic knowledge but also the skills necessary to contribute to contemporary society.
The IHE curriculum focuses on the rigorous study of classical Islamic texts, providing students with direct access to the rich intellectual heritage of Islamic scholarship. Students engage deeply with foundational works in Hadith, Fiqh, Tafsir, and other essential disciplines, ensuring that they acquire a strong grounding in Islamic jurisprudence, theology, and spirituality. The aim is to train students in the scholarly methods of traditional Islamic learning while also equipping them to apply these principles to modern-day contexts and challenges. This approach enables our students to think critically and responsibly, navigating the modern world while remaining anchored in Islamic teachings.
A key feature of the programme is its emphasis on the study of classical texts, some of which have shaped Islamic scholarship for centuries. By studying these revered works, students gain insights into how Islamic scholars approached theology, law, and ethics throughout history. The curriculum also encourages students to reflect on how these classical teachings apply to contemporary issues, helping them develop the intellectual tools needed to serve their communities and guide others in navigating the challenges of modern life.
In addition to academic and intellectual development, our Islamic Higher Education curriculum places great emphasis on spiritual and moral formation. Students are encouraged to cultivate their character, learning to embody the values of justice, compassion, and integrity that are central to Islamic teachings. Leadership skills are also nurtured, as students are trained to become positive role models and community leaders, capable of guiding others with wisdom and clarity.
In summary, the Islamic Higher Education curriculum at Darul Hadis Latifiah is designed to produce individuals who are not only well-versed in the classical Islamic sciences but also equipped to apply their knowledge in a modern context. Our goal is to develop future Ulama (scholars) and leaders who can lead their communities with both religious insight and practical competence, ensuring that the rich legacy of Islamic scholarship continues to thrive in the modern world.

pageCache.text:
Empowering the Future: Islamic Education in the UK
Islamic education has long been a cornerstone of personal and community development within Muslim societies. Its central tenet is the holistic nurturing of both the intellect and the soul, promoting ethical and spiritual growth alongside academic achievement. In the UK, with its diverse and multicultural population, Islamic education plays an increasingly important role in empowering the next generation of Muslims. Through madrasas, Islamic schools, and educational programs, the Muslim community is ensuring that its youth are well-equipped to navigate the complexities of modern life while staying grounded in their faith.
The Importance of Islamic Education
Islamic education goes beyond simply teaching religious texts. It seeks to instill a sense of purpose, moral responsibility, and a deep connection to one’s spiritual identity. For Muslims, knowledge is seen as a form of worship, with numerous references in the Qur’an and Hadith encouraging the pursuit of learning. Islamic education, therefore, encompasses not only the study of Islamic principles but also the development of strong character traits such as compassion, integrity, and justice.
In the UK, where Muslims represent a significant portion of the population, Islamic education provides an essential link between the younger generation and their cultural and religious heritage. With increasing secularism and the challenges of integration, Islamic schools and madrasas offer a space where Muslim children can cultivate a strong sense of self while receiving a high-quality education. This dual focus on religious and academic excellence helps prepare students for future success in a wide range of careers and social roles.
The Role of Madrasas in the UK
Madrasas have traditionally been the heart of Islamic education, particularly in Muslim-majority countries. In the UK, they serve a similar function, offering supplementary education to children outside of regular school hours. Often attached to mosques, madrasas provide instruction in Qur’anic studies, Arabic language, Islamic history, and Fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence).
For many British Muslims, the madrasa is a community hub where children not only learn religious knowledge but also build relationships with peers and elders. The environment fosters a sense of belonging, which is vital for young Muslims growing up in a predominantly non-Muslim society. Furthermore, madrasas offer a space for parents to ensure their children are receiving guidance aligned with their values, which may not always be provided in mainstream schools.
However, like any educational institution, madrasas face challenges. There has been a growing need for modernization in teaching methods and curriculum design to meet the needs of today’s learners. While traditional methods of rote memorization and strict discipline were once effective, there is a rising demand for more interactive and engaging teaching styles that foster critical thinking and creativity. Many madrasas in the UK are now incorporating modern pedagogical approaches, such as digital tools and project-based learning, to better equip students for the future.
Islamic Schools: Balancing Faith and Academic Excellence
Beyond madrasas, full-time Islamic schools have become an increasingly popular option for Muslim families in the UK. These institutions offer a balanced curriculum, blending secular education with Islamic studies. The appeal of Islamic schools lies in their ability to create an environment where students can practice their faith freely while excelling academically.
Many Islamic schools in the UK are known for their strong academic performance, often exceeding national averages in key subjects such as mathematics, science, and English. These schools also prioritize Islamic values in their ethos, promoting ethical behavior, charity, and community service alongside academic achievement. For parents, Islamic schools provide a level of assurance that their children are learning in a setting that reflects their cultural and religious beliefs, shielding them from potential conflicts in secular schools.
However, the success of Islamic schools in the UK depends largely on maintaining high standards of education while staying true to their religious mission. Some schools have faced challenges in balancing the requirements of the UK’s national curriculum with the expectations of Islamic studies. Yet, many have found innovative ways to integrate both, ensuring that students leave with a well-rounded education that prepares them for life in both the Muslim and broader British communities.
Islamic Education in the Digital Age
As technology continues to reshape the educational landscape, Islamic education in the UK is also evolving. Online platforms and digital resources are now playing a significant role in supplementing traditional forms of learning. Whether through Qur’an apps, online Islamic courses, or virtual madrasas, technology is making Islamic education more accessible to a wider audience.
This digital transformation is particularly important for Muslim families who may not have access to a nearby madrasa or Islamic school. With online learning, students can study Qur’an recitation, Hadith, and other Islamic subjects from the comfort of their homes. Additionally, digital platforms offer flexible learning schedules, making it easier for working parents to support their children’s religious education.
The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated this shift towards digital learning, and many madrasas and Islamic schools in the UK have continued to integrate online tools even after reopening their doors. This hybrid approach to Islamic education is likely to become a permanent feature, offering students more personalized and flexible learning opportunities.
Empowering the Future: The Impact of Islamic Education
The role of Islamic education in empowering future generations cannot be overstated. By providing young Muslims with a strong foundation in both religious knowledge and academic excellence, Islamic schools and madrasas are equipping them to thrive in a multicultural and fast-changing world. These institutions not only help preserve Islamic identity but also foster a sense of civic responsibility and global citizenship.
Moreover, the values instilled through Islamic education—compassion, honesty, justice—are universally relevant, preparing students to contribute positively to both the Muslim community and wider society. As Islamic education continues to evolve in the UK, it will play a crucial role in shaping a generation of confident, informed, and morally grounded individuals ready to lead and serve in various capacities.
In conclusion, Islamic education in the UK is empowering the next generation of Muslims by nurturing their intellectual, spiritual, and moral development. Whether through traditional madrasas, Islamic schools, or digital learning platforms, the future of Islamic education is bright, offering young people the tools they need to succeed in both their faith and the modern world.
